confluences.description: Warpaint is the rite of the war band: ochre and blood smeared into runes that bind fighters to one another before they march. Bearers have streaks of colour that never quite wash out of their skin, and their magic flashes in the same jagged stripes.

grant.name: War Marks
grant.text: Once per long rest, you can spend 10 minutes painting war marks on up to six willing creatures, which can include yourself. For the next 8 hours, each marked creature knows the direction of every other marked creature that is within 1 mile of it.

confluences.name: Warren
confluences.theme: Burrows with a dozen escape holes
confluences.description: Warren is the rabbit city under the meadow, a maze of tunnels with a bolt-hole for every danger, teeming with life and quick to empty. A bearer grows lean and twitchy-nosed, always sits where they can see the door, and their spells dart away in quick zigzags and vanish into the ground.

grant.name: Bolt-Hole
grant.text: Whenever you are inside a building, cave, tunnel or walled place, you know the direction of its nearest way out other than the way you came in.

confluences.name: Watchman
confluences.theme: Lantern and call through sleeping streets
confluences.description: The watchman walks the dark streets with lantern and hand bell, calling the hours and crying the alarm when trouble comes. Bearers have a carrying voice and a habit of glancing over their shoulders, a faint glow lingers about them at night, and their magic rings out like a bell.

grant.name: Walking the Beat
grant.text: When you walk along a street, corridor or path that you have walked within the last 7 days, you automatically notice anything that has changed there since, such as a forced lock, a new mark on a door, a moved crate or a missing sign.

confluences.name: Weaver
confluences.theme: Threads, webs and woven patterns
confluences.description: Weaver is the spinner's patience fused with the web and the knotted line. Bearers' fingers are never still, picking at threads and tying tiny knots, and their spells unspool in fine glowing strands that cross into patterns.

grant.name: Thread-Sense
grant.text: While you touch a web, net, rope or thread, you feel anything else that touches or tugs on it anywhere along its length, and you know roughly how far along it that is.

confluences.name: Wergild
confluences.theme: A life's worth weighed in coin
confluences.description: Wergild is the blood price, the old law that a killing or a maiming can be weighed, judged and paid in silver rather than answered with more blood. Bearers carry themselves like arbiters, talk easily of debts and honour, and their magic chimes like coins dropping onto a balance pan.

grant.name: Blood Money
grant.text: You have advantage on Charisma (Persuasion) checks made to settle a feud, grudge or blood debt through payment, apology or ransom, whether you negotiate for yourself or on another's behalf.

confluences.name: Whaler
confluences.theme: Hunting giants under open sail
confluences.description: The whaler sails far out under wind and weather to hunt beasts larger than the ship, trusting a harpoon, a line and a strong back. Bearers are weathered and steady-handed, smell faintly of tar and lamp oil, and their magic lashes out and holds like a barbed line.

grant.name: Hold Fast
grant.text: You have advantage on Strength checks made to haul, pull or hold on to a rope, chain or line, such as reeling in a harpooned beast, keeping a boat moored in a strong current, or holding an ally who is dangling from a cliff.

confluences.name: Whirlwind
confluences.theme: Spinning blades in a storm
confluences.description: The whirlwind is the warrior who never stands still, all spinning steel and sudden gusts. Bearers turn on their heels while they talk and dust swirls around their feet, and their spells spin out in tight spirals of wind and glinting light.

grant.name: Whirling Step
grant.text: Once per short rest, when a creature misses you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to move up to 5 feet without provoking opportunity attacks.

confluences.name: White Hart
confluences.theme: The pale quarry no hunter catches
confluences.description: The white hart is the shining stag of hunting legend, always glimpsed between the trees and never brought down, leading its pursuers toward quests rather than kills. Bearers grow lean and graceful with pale streaks in their hair, and their magic leaves glowing hoofprints that fade within a heartbeat.

grant.name: Never Caught
grant.text: You have advantage on ability checks and saving throws made to avoid or escape nets, snares, bolas, pits and hunting traps.

confluences.name: Wight
confluences.theme: Dead warriors bound to their arms
confluences.description: Wights are dead warriors held in their barrows by dark magic, still clutching sword and shield. Bearers have a cold grip and a pale, grave-dust complexion, old armour feels like home to them, and their magic smells of cold iron and burial mounds.

grant.name: Last Hand
grant.text: Once per long rest, you can hold a weapon, shield or piece of armour for 1 minute to see a brief vision of the last time someone died while wielding or wearing it: where it happened, roughly when, and what killed them. If no one ever has, you learn that instead.

confluences.name: Wild Hunt
confluences.theme: Spectral riders on the night gale
confluences.description: The Wild Hunt is the ghostly host that gallops across the sky on stormy nights, with baying hounds and riders no one can see clearly. Bearers grow restless after dusk and love to ride hard in the dark, their cloaks and hair stream in winds that aren't blowing, and their magic sweeps past in a rush of hoofbeats and cold air.

grant.name: Night Gallop
grant.text: When you travel overland between dusk and dawn, you and any companions travelling with you cover ground as if moving at a fast pace while actually moving at a normal pace.

confluences.name: Wildfire
confluences.theme: Flames racing faster than horses
confluences.description: The wildfire that leaps from treetop to treetop and outruns riders across dry grass. Bearers are quick, impatient and hard to pin down, their hair lifts as if in a hot updraft, and their magic spreads in racing tongues of light.

grant.name: Read the Blaze
grant.text: When you can see a fire, you know which way and how fast it will spread over the next hour, and the quickest safe route out of its path.

confluences.name: Windmill
confluences.theme: Turning sails that grind the grain
confluences.description: Windmill is the strength of the wind harnessed to feed a village, great sails turning day and night to grind the harvest into flour. A bearer has broad, tireless shoulders and flour-dusted hands, works in a steady, unbroken rhythm, and their spells turn and sweep in great slow circles.

grant.name: Work Song
grant.text: When you sing or chant while using the Help action to aid another creature's Strength check, that creature also adds your proficiency bonus to the roll.

confluences.name: Windseller
confluences.theme: Fair winds sold in knotted cords
confluences.description: The windseller is the old sea witch on the harbour steps who ties breezes into knotted string and sells them to sailors at a steep price. Bearers smell of salt and hemp and always have a length of knotted cord about them, and their spells untwist with a sudden gust off the water.

grant.name: Knotted Wind
grant.text: Once per long rest, you can spend 10 minutes whistling as you tie a knot in a cord. Any creature holding the cord can untie the knot as an action to make a steady breeze blow in a direction of its choice within 1 mile of it for 1 hour, unless a storm is raging there. The breeze is strong enough to fill a sail but not to harm or push anyone. The knot loses its power at your next long rest if it hasn't been untied.

confluences.name: Wishing Well
confluences.theme: Coins dropped into deep water
confluences.description: Wishing Well is the old stone well in the village square where coins glint at the bottom and whispered hopes sometimes come true. A bearer always seems to have a spare copper to toss, their voice echoes faintly as if spoken down a shaft, and their magic falls away with a soft splash and a ripple of light.

grant.name: Penny Wish
grant.text: Once per long rest, you can drop a coin into a well, fountain, spring or pool and whisper a wish. Before your next long rest, you can add 1d4 to one ability check you make that directly helps that wish come true.

confluences.name: Witch
confluences.theme: Hedge magic of herbs and blood
confluences.description: Old craft brewed from roots, leaves and a drop of the brewer's own blood: the hedge-healer's charm and the village curse alike. Bearers keep their pockets full of dried herbs and their fingertips stained green, and their magic curls up like steam from a simmering pot.

grant.name: Hedge Remedy
grant.text: Once per long rest, you can spend 10 minutes brewing herbs and a drop of your blood into a draught. A creature that drinks it within the next 24 hours has advantage on the next saving throw it makes against poison or disease within 8 hours of drinking it.

confluences.name: Wrecker
confluences.theme: False lights luring ships onto rocks
confluences.description: The wrecker waits on the cliffs on stormy nights, swinging a lantern to lure ships onto the rocks and then plundering whatever washes ashore. Bearers have a sly, patient look and salt-cracked hands, and their spells flicker like a lantern seen through rain.

grant.name: Wrecker's Lantern
grant.text: As an action, you can touch a nonmagical light source, such as a lantern, torch or campfire, and change the colour of its light and make it flicker, pulse or shine steadily in any pattern you choose. The change lasts until you use this trait again or the light goes out. Seen from more than 100 feet away, the light can pass for a lighthouse, a signal lamp, a lit window or any other ordinary light.

confluences.name: Wyvern
confluences.theme: Venomous raider of the crags
confluences.description: The wyvern is the two-legged dragon of the high crags, all wings, claws and a venomous tail, that swoops down to carry off sheep and soldiers alike. Bearers grow lean and powerful through the shoulders, their skin takes a faint scaled sheen, and their magic strikes from above with a rush of leathery wings.

grant.name: Venom-Blooded
grant.text: You have advantage on saving throws against poison delivered by a bite or a sting.

confluences.name: Yeoman
confluences.theme: Farmers who defend their own fields
confluences.description: Yeoman is the free farmer who works the land in peace and takes up a pitchfork when raiders come. A bearer has broad, work-roughened hands and a sun-browned neck, can judge a field's yield at a glance, and their magic feels as solid and dependable as a well-kept plough.

grant.name: Pitchfork Militia
grant.text: You are proficient with improvised weapons made from farm and garden tools, such as pitchforks, scythes, flails, sickles, hoes and wood axes.

confluences.name: Yew
confluences.theme: Graveyard tree of death and longbows
confluences.description: The yew is the dark-needled tree of old graveyards, poisonous in every part, whose roots drink from the graves and whose wood bends into the strongest war bows. Bearers grow tough and slow to tire, their skin takes on the reddish brown of yew bark, and their magic creaks and flexes like a drawn bow.

grant.name: Sound Wood
grant.text: By flexing, rapping or running your hand along a wooden object for a moment, such as a bow, a spear shaft, a ladder, a beam or a mast, you know whether it is sound, and you find any rot, hidden crack, worm damage or deliberate sabotage in it.

confluences.name: Zealot
confluences.theme: Burning faith that bleeds for its cause
confluences.description: Holy conviction set on fire and paid for in blood: the believer who will march into any battle. Bearers speak with a fervent heat and their eyes shine a little too bright, and their magic burns with a white-gold flame streaked with red.

grant.name: Rousing Sermon
grant.text: Once per long rest, you can spend 10 minutes preaching to up to six creatures that can hear and understand you. For the next hour, each of them has advantage on the first saving throw it makes against being frightened.

confluences.name: Zenith
confluences.theme: Noon light with nowhere to hide
confluences.description: Zenith is light at its fullest and most honest, the noonday sun that leaves no shadow and no falsehood. A bearer's shadow is always small and pale beneath them, their gaze is hard to meet for long, and their spells strike with a flat white glare.

grant.name: Noonday Glare
grant.text: Once per long rest, as an action, you can blaze with white light for 1 minute, shedding bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for a further 30 feet. Any illusion created by a spell of 1st level or lower, such as disguise self or silent image, that is within your bright light flickers visibly, and every creature that sees it knows it is an illusion.

confluences.name: Zephyr
confluences.theme: Airy spirit of drafts and breezes
confluences.description: The zephyr is the gentle west wind given a mind of its own, a quick, unseen spirit that slips through every gap and keyhole. Bearers seem slightly too light on their feet, their hair and clothes stir in breezes no one else feels, and their spells arrive with a soft rush of air that rustles pages and flickers candles.

grant.name: Draft-Sense
grant.text: You can feel the faintest movement of air. You have advantage on checks made to find hidden doors, vents, shafts and other passages that have air flowing through them, and to find the way out of an enclosed place by following a draft.

confluences.name: Time
confluences.theme: Moments stretched, stopped and stolen
confluences.description: Time held in the hand. Bearers are never late and never hurried, and the world around them seems to pause, very briefly, when they decide something matters.

grant.name: Stolen Second
grant.text: Once per long rest, at the end of another creature's turn, you can take one action immediately.
